summary.headline: Priced near the top of its 5-year range and above peers
summary.takeaway: Investors pay more for each dollar of Apple's profit and sales than in most of the last 5 years, and far more than similar companies. Profit growth of about 13.6% a year only partly explains this higher price.

positives.text: EPS (profit per share) grew 13.6% over the past year, matching its 3-year yearly average of 13.6%. Growth has been steady.
Forward P/E is 33.4, lower than today's 39.5. This is based on analysts' estimates of higher profit next fiscal year.

watch_outs.text: P/E (price compared with yearly profit) is 39.5, higher than 96% of the last 5 years and almost double the peer median of 20.8.
PEG (P/E compared with expected growth) is 3.18. The price is high relative to the 12.4% profit growth analysts estimate.
Revenue grew 11.7% over the past year, well below the peer median of 46.6%, while P/S is 10.7 versus peers' 2.58.

what_to_watch_next: Next earnings report on 29 Jan 2027, which will update profit growth behind the P/E.
P/E of 39.5 is close to its 5-year high of 42.6 and well above its 5-year median of 31.6.
summary.ask_yourself: How comfortable are you paying a price well above the company's usual level for its current growth?
